data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"On a random 3-regular graph with asynchronous majority dynamics from a uniform random two-coloring, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus as n grows tends to a constant strictly between 0 and 1 (bounded away from both 0 and 1). The obstruction structures are locally stable mixed configurations: colorings in which every vertex agrees with at least two of its three neighbors, so no vertex ever changes its opinion. In any minimal such mixed configuration the disagreeing edges form a matching (each vertex has exactly one neighbor of the opposite color and two of the same), i.e. the vertex set decomposes into monochromatic induced components pairwise joined by a perfect matching of cross edges. Their prevalence follows a falsifiable quantitative law: the dynamics converges whp to a locally stable configuration whose expected number of disagreeing-edge pairs is \u0398(n), proportional to n with a positive constant times n density; consensus (zero pairs) is a large-deviation event with probability strictly between 0 and 1, so the consensus probability approaches a nondegenerate constant, and the count of dissenting pairs per vertex converges to a Poisson-free positive constant independent of n.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the disagreeing-edge matching can always be dissolved by correlated chains of updates (a vertex with two same-colored neighbors of the opposite color flipping), the bounded-below claim fails and consensus probability tends to 1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expected number of surviving dissenting pairs were o(n) or exponentially small in n, the constant-verdict fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If random 3-regular graphs whp admit a global potential argument forcing energy to zero, consensus probability \u2192 1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the absorbing set includes period-2 cycles rather than only fixed points, the obstruction characterization must be widened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Each asynchronous update moves a vertex to the local majority of its three neighbors, which can only decrease the number of disagreeing edges incident to it or create new ones on the other side; on a 3-regular graph a vertex is stable exactly when at most one neighbor disagrees with it. Absorbing states of the dynamics are exactly the locally stable configurations, which include consensus but also mixed states where the disagreeing-edge subgraph has maximum degree 1 (a matching): flipping any single vertex would then put it in the minority of its neighborhood, so it never flips under majority rule. Starting from a uniform coloring, an \u03a9(n) fraction of vertices sit in stable local patches, and the asynchronous dynamics eliminates unstable vertices in O(n log n) expected steps while being unable to dissolve a matching of cross edges once each side is internally monochromatic; hence the limiting state is mixed with probability bounded below by a constant, giving a consensus probability strictly between 0 and 1 as n \u2192 \u221e.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
